title: Non-Hermitian photonic time quasicrystal
authors: Shuhang Chen, Zhi Zheng, Qi Zhu
abstract: Photonic time crystals amplify waves through temporal modulation. We study a temporal analogue of the non-Hermitian Aubry-André-Harper model. By continuing an incommensurate temporal modulation into the complex phase plane, we find that the bulk amplification rate as a function of the complexification coordinate is organized into distinct integer phases, with its slope locked to an integer within each phase. This integer is Avila's acceleration, connecting a global structure of quasiperiodic operator theory with a directly observable optical propagation response. The quantized response persists in the presence of defects in the time-dependent permittivity modulation that preserve the underlying analytic phase structure. As a wave-level consequence, two input frequencies belonging to different integer phases acquire exponentially separated amplification, producing spectral selection and reshaping the temporal beat pattern. Our results establish that a global integer of quasiperiodic operator theory can govern a tunable, quantized growth response in a non-Hermitian photonic time quasicrystal.
summary: This work investigates non-Hermitian photonic time quasicrystals, showing that their amplification rate is governed by a global integer invariant derived from quasiperiodic operator theory. The integer phase dictates a quantized growth response, leading to spectral selection. This establishes a powerful link between abstract mathematical invariants and measurable optical properties.
main_problem: To establish a connection between a global integer invariant from quasiperiodic operator theory (Avila's acceleration) and a directly observable optical propagation response in a non-Hermitian photonic time quasicrystal.
main_result: The bulk amplification rate exhibits plateaus where its derivative is quantized to an integer $n$, demonstrating that a global integer invariant governs a tunable, quantized growth response.
method: The analysis uses the transfer matrix method applied to the wave equation, connecting the Lyapunov exponent calculation to the theory of quasiperiodic cocycles.
model_or_system: The system is a Non-Hermitian Photonic Time Quasicrystal (NH-PTQC) modeled by a wave equation with a complex, quasiperiodically modulated permittivity $\epsilon_m$. The dynamics are governed by a transfer matrix product.
key_observables: Bulk logarithmic amplification rate ($g_\infty(h)$), the integer slope of this rate ($\partial_+ h g_\infty = n \in \mathbb{Z}$), and the output power ratio between two input frequencies.
important_parameters: The complexification coordinate $h$, the modulation frequency $\alpha$, and the defect strength $\eta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the permittivity avoids zero, defining a nonsingular strip, and that the underlying analytic phase structure is preserved even in the presence of defects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the NH-PTQC structure, the quantization of the amplification rate's slope into integer phases, and phase diagrams mapping these integer phases in the parameter space.
paper_structure: The paper develops the connection between the quasiperiodic operator theory (Avila's acceleration) and the optical response by analyzing the Lyapunov exponent via transfer matrices. It then explores the robustness of this integer quantization against defects and examines the spectral selection resulting from different input frequencies belonging to different integer phases.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete physical realization (photonic crystals) where a deep mathematical concept (quasiperiodic operator theory invariants) dictates a measurable, quantized physical response (amplification rate), bridging abstract mathematics with applied optics.
